sql: MERGE INTO s.t AS tgt USING s.t2 AS src ON tgt.id = src.t_id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET name = src.label RETURNING WITH (OLD AS prev, NEW AS curr) prev.name AS before_name, curr.name AS after_name
note: RETURNING WITH named OLD/NEW aliases and output aliases

sql: MERGE INTO s.t2 AS tgt USING (SELECT id, name FROM s.t WHERE val > 0) AS src ON tgt.t_id = src.id WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (t_id, label) VALUES (src.id, src.name) WHEN MATCHED AND tgt.label IS DISTINCT FROM src.name THEN UPDATE SET label = src.name
note: USING filtered source, NOT MATCHED INSERT before MATCHED UPDATE, IS DISTINCT FROM condition

sql: MERGE INTO s.t AS tgt USING s.t2 AS src ON tgt.id = src.t_id WHEN MATCHED AND tgt.status IN ('sad', 'ok') THEN UPDATE SET status = 'happy'

sql: MERGE INTO s.t AS tgt USING s.t2 AS src ON tgt.id = src.t_id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET name = src.label RETURNING WITH (OLD AS o, NEW AS n) n.id, o.name AS old_name, n.name AS new_name, merge_action()
